answers.core:
Direct integration with the audio system: It needs to interact at a low level with Godot's audio system to manage music and FX channels, which would be more difficult to achieve with an external add-on.

Key feature for retro projects: It is highly useful for retro or educational game developers, benefiting Godot by offering unique functionality out of the box.

Better user experience: Users wouldn’t need to search for or configure plugins, simplifying the development process for those making retro games with synthesized audio.

Performance optimization: Being integrated into the core allows the system to be optimized for better performance without the overhead that an add-on might bring.

Consistency with other Godot features: Just like the physics and graphics engines, having this feature in the core creates a more cohesive experience for developers.

Cross-platform support: Core integration ensures it will work properly across all platforms where Godot is available (mobile, desktop, web).
